name: tangie

attributes.attribute: Scottish sea spirit that haunts fresh and salt water
shifts between the shape of a human and a water horse

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The tangie is a Scottish spirit of the shore. It appeared beside fresh and salt water on the Orkney islands. The form changed from one sighting to the next. At times it looked like a person. At other times it took the shape of a fierce water horse. The name comes from a local word for seaweed, tang. The tale of the tangie stayed a mystery of the northern shoreline.

okr.objective: Record the tangie as a shape-shifting Scottish sea spirit.
key_results: Places the tangie by fresh and salt water on the Orkney islands
Notes it shifts between a human and a water horse
Derives the name from the word tang, meaning seaweed
